title: The wolf and the lamb (Isaiah 11:1–9)
hookLine: a shoot from Jesse's root; the Church draws its seven gifts of the Spirit from this chapter

lines: A STUMP, LOW TO THE GROUND.
A SHOOT FROM THE ROOT OF JESSE.
cards: A stump. Nothing left of the tree but a stump, low to the ground, the kind you'd trip over. Some readers see the royal family of David in it: once a great tree, now cut down.
And then, in the Douay-Rheims: "there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root." A green shoot from a dead stump.
Jesse was David's father, the man whose youngest son was out with the sheep. In Advent, some Catholic families hang ornaments on a Jesse tree, and this is the verse it grows from.

teach.b: Isaiah says what will rest on this new king.

In the Douay: "the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, the spirit of counsel, and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge, and of godliness," and he shall be filled "with the spirit of the fear of the Lord."
Count them: seven. That's where the Church's list of the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit comes from: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord.
Readers of the Hebrew point out that it names only six: fear of the Lord appears twice.

teach.h: SIX IN HEBREW, SEVEN IN LATIN.
teach.b: The Greek and Latin translators rendered the first one as godliness, or piety, and so the list became seven. Christians read the shoot from Jesse as Christ, on whom the Spirit rests completely.
And the Catechism teaches that these same gifts are given to every Christian, sealed especially in confirmation, as steady dispositions that make a person ready to follow the Spirit's lead.
Then the chapter's picture of this king's reign.

teach.h: THE WOLF SHALL DWELL WITH THE LAMB.
teach.b: "The wolf shall dwell with the lamb: and the leopard shall lie down with the kid," calf and lion together, "and a little child shall lead them." A toddler plays by a snake's hole and isn't hurt.

teach.h: THE SPIRIT OF WISDOM, AND OF UNDERSTANDING.
teach.b: The saying goes that the lion will lie down with the lamb. Isaiah actually pairs the wolf with the lamb, and the lion with the calf.
When the earth is full of the knowledge of the Lord, the old enemies stop hurting each other.

how: Catholics are sealed with the gifts of the Holy Spirit in confirmation, many families keep a Jesse tree through Advent, and Isaiah 11 is read at Mass in Advent, including the Second Sunday of Advent in one year of the cycle.

games.q: the shoot of Jesse — tap the pairs.

s: Isaiah says the lion shall lie down with the lamb
he pairs the wolf with the lamb, the leopard with the kid, and the calf with the lion.
the Hebrew text names the fear of the Lord twice
Greek and Latin translators made the first one piety, giving seven gifts.
the Jesse tree comes from this chapter
a rod out of the root of Jesse: the shoot from David's family stump.

games.q: you're reading Isaiah 11 in Hebrew and counting the spirits that rest on the shoot of Jesse. how many do you count?
o: six, with fear of the Lord twice.
games.why: the Hebrew has six, with fear of the Lord repeated. the Greek and Latin rendered one as piety, and the Church's list became seven.

practice: Let the seven pass through your mind, wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, fear of the Lord, and see if one catches: counsel for a decision, fortitude for something you dread, understanding for a person who baffles you.
If you pray, ask the Holy Spirit for that one gift, simply, by name; if you don't, hold the word and picture your week with more of it.

wordCard.voice: netser. Hebrew for branch, shoot: the green shoot from the stump of Jesse that Isaiah says will carry the sevenfold spirit of the Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: branch, shoot. The netser that grows out of Jesse's roots in Isaiah 11:1.
